reason: Build haemoglobin in the developing red cells to give the blood an oxygen carrier.
expectation: The cells will make haemoglobin from the supplied materials, though I don't know how the result will depict it.

alternatives.reason: Plasma is also needed for the sample, but I want to start with oxygen transport.

effect: The result shows haemoglobin assembling in developing cells and their maturation into nucleus-free red cells; oxygen can now be added.
reaction: The maturation arrow is useful, though the loss of the nucleus is not explained.
reason: Add oxygen to see how the red cells carry it.
expectation: Oxygen will bind to haemoglobin in the red cells, perhaps with a depiction of its release.

alternatives.reason: Plasma is needed for the blood sample, but I want to follow the oxygen-carrying cells first.

effect: The result shows reversible oxygen binding and explains why more oxygen leaves haemoglobin in working tissues. I can now assemble the plasma.
reaction: The link between low dissolved oxygen and release is useful.
reason: Make plasma for the blood sample; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: The water and solutes will form plasma, though I don't know how it will be depicted.

effect: Plasma is ready to receive the blood cells.
reaction: The picture shows its dissolved components, but adds little beyond the ingredients.
reason: Add the oxygen-bearing red cells to assemble the oxygen-carrying sample.
expectation: The red cells will be suspended in plasma; the white cells and platelets may still need adding.

alternatives.reason: White cells and platelets belong in the sample too, but the current goal emphasizes oxygen transport.

effect: The red cells are suspended in plasma, but the sample still lacks white cells and platelets.
reaction: The partial-sample picture makes the remaining components clear.
reason: Add the missing white cells and platelets; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: The result will be a blood sample containing plasma, oxygen-bearing red cells, white cells and platelets.

effect: The completed sample brings the blood components together and distinguishes plasma's transport role from the red cells' oxygen-carrying role.
reaction: The planned magnified inset usefully connects the whole sample back to haemoglobin.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding oxygen to red cells was most worthwhile: the planned picture shows reversible binding, and the prose connects release to low dissolved oxygen in working tissues.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making plasma felt least informative: the planned picture showed particles and proteins but added little about their roles. The loss of the red-cell nucleus during maturation was also shown without explanation.

surprise.text: The explanation that more oxygen can leave haemoglobin where dissolved oxygen is low clarified how the carrier can supply working tissues.

arbitrary.text: No combination felt purposeless, although the final addition left the functions of white cells and platelets unexplained. The compatible-option menu guided the choices, so I did not discover the recipes independently.

continue.text: I would continue to see how circulation connects these oxygen carriers to the arm's cells; the release explanation made that next connection interesting.
